newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Just Jeans says behind budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Just Jeans says behind budget.

text.p: Clothing retailer Just Jeans Holdings Ltd said on Friday that it was behind budget for its summer season and that retailing conditions remained difficult.

"The current retail market continues to be very difficult and as a result, our summer opening has been disappointing, and in the early part of the season we are falling short of budget," managing director Peter Wilkinson said.
Earlier, Just Jeans reported a net profit of A$14.11 million for the year to July 27, up from A$12.65 million a year earlier.
Sales rose to A$340.48 million from A$315.95 million.
"In summer, we had a good solid season. Winter, however, once again proved to be very difficult," Wilkinson said.
"The retail market was weak in the lead up to the federal election (on March 2), and despite expectations otherwise, continued to deteriorate after the election," he said in a statement.
"In this environment we experienced significant pressure on turnover and margins," he said.
"So it was pleasing that despite these conditions the Group improved winter pre-tax profit by 15 percent over last year."
Wilkinson said that particularly welcome was the improvement in the performance of the group's Jacqui E chain.
"Whilst Jacqui E continued to incur losses, performance did improve significantly in the second half," he said.
"The enormous effort in repositioning the business coupled with better focussed merchandise strategies and logistic continue into the new financial year," he said.
"Jay Jays Trademark has had a good year with sales and profit growth meeting expectations," he said.
Store numbers increased to 60 from 45 by the end of July. "We plan to open another 20 stores in 1996/97," Wilkinson said.
Wilkinson said the group had maintained a very tight control of stock levels and it did not expect any severe problems from overstocking.
Just Jeans shares were untraded on Friday after closing at A$2.20 on Thursday.
